extracted.intended_audience: research funders, research-policy makers, research integrity scholars and funder staff
extracted.subtask_description: Synthesis and evaluation of interventions to improve peer review and funding decision-making (process, reviewer selection, scoring, and applicant burden). Focuses on what changes funders and stakeholders implemented and the short- and long-term outcomes observed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of decision-support software / performance matrix
rubrics_metrics.description: Use software (e.g., ProGrid, Teamworker) to evaluate applications based on a ‘performance matrix’ of researcher/proposal variables.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported benefits include shorter meetings, fairer proposal discussions, and simplified decision-making. Practical implementation requires appropriate configuration and may change meeting dynamics; caveats about replacing human judgement are implied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correlate review scores with applicant CV data to predict success
rubrics_metrics.description: Correlate review scores with applicant CV data to predict likelihood of research success and rank applicants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Found to be reliable in some settings (especially fellowships where CV emphasis is appropriate) but requires high alignment between institutions and high-quality CV data; should be used as adjunct rather than a replacement for peer review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Streamlining: shorter applications and simplified scoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Shorter applications and simplified scoring systems to reduce applicant, reviewer and funder workload.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shortening applications decreased writing and review time and sped up decisions. Agreement between standard and simplified systems was sometimes below acceptable thresholds (e.g., <75%), so benchmarks for success must be defined and validated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision-support models using bibliometric data
rubrics_metrics.description: Create funding decision support models that use bibliometric indicators (citation indices, publication records) to aid selection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Can improve administrative efficiency and supplement reviewer judgement but differences in classification systems, field coverage, and potential biases mean bibliometric models should be adjunctive and carefully audited for bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer registries built from bibliometric data / semi-automatic selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Create reviewers’ registries and semi-automatic reviewer selection tools based on bibliometric indicators (PMIDs, MeSH, citation indices).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Saved programme officer time and improved matching in pilots, but practical issues include heterogeneous classification systems, reviewer non-participation, possible performance-bias signals, and uneven disciplinary coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer training to reduce bias and increase interrater reliability
rubrics_metrics.description: Training reviewers on assessment criteria and good review practices to improve reliability and reduce bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training has shown potential to reduce bias and increase interrater reliability in some studies; implementation requires resources and evaluation of training effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical determination of number of reviewers per application (NIH: ~4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use statistical analysis to determine optimal number of reviewers per proposal; NIH simulation suggested four reviewers as a minimum appropriate number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: More reviewers can increase reliability, particularly for contentious applications, but implementing a higher number is administratively and financially challenging; pragmatic compromises (e.g., ≥3) may be recommended for smaller funders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use multidisciplinary panels
rubrics_metrics.description: Assemble review panels with multidisciplinary expertise to improve selection fairness and consensus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended to improve reliability and breadth of judgement; may require expanded reviewer pools and careful panel design to avoid dilution of subject expertise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid researcher-nominated reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not rely on researcher-nominated reviewers for assessments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Removing researcher nominations was recommended to reduce bias and enhance impartiality in reviewer selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Increase reviews per proposal / assign more proposals to reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Assign more reviewers per proposal and/or more proposals per reviewer to improve interrater agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ARC recommended more reviewers and assigning multiple proposals per reviewer to improve agreement; however, this can exacerbate reviewer fatigue and administrative burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use a smaller core of highly selected reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Concentrate most reviews in a smaller number of well-selected reviewers within subdisciplines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May increase consistency and quality of reviews, but concentrated workloads can increase fatigue and the risk of over-dependence on few experts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant involvement in peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Have applicants review proposals competing for the same funds (e.g., pilots where applicants rank several competing proposals).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pilots reported motivated review pools and comparable review quality by some metrics; concerns include potential group consensus effects that may discourage innovation and limited evaluation beyond interrater agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Virtual panel meetings as alternative to face-to-face
rubrics_metrics.description: Use teleconference/virtual panels to conduct peer review meetings instead of face-to-face.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evidence shows little difference in scoring, discussion time, or reliability in some settings and reduced travel costs; requires investment in technology and supports and may depend on number of reviewers per application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission quotas to reduce application demand
rubrics_metrics.description: Introduce submission quotas for HEIs or applicants to reduce the number of applications funders must process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quotas can reduce funder workload but may shift burden to institutional internal peer review and create unintended administrative consequences; success may depend on HEI-level processes to manage internal reviews constructively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant anonymity / blind review
rubrics_metrics.description: Mask applicant identity (names, affiliations, publications) during review to focus assessment on proposal merit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pilot evidence (NSF, Villum Foundation) suggests anonymity increased willingness to propose risky ideas and reduced bias, leading to funding of different candidate sets; anonymity can be combined with other methods for greater effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer 'Golden ticket' autonomy
rubrics_metrics.description: Allow reviewers a discretionary nomination ('golden ticket') to champion one proposal regardless of formal criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Villum Foundation example awarded ~31% of grants via golden tickets in a cycle; can promote reviewer autonomy and fund high-risk innovative ideas but may reduce transparency if unregulated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awards to exceptional investigators / no-strings funding
rubrics_metrics.description: Create funding streams aimed at exceptional investigators (e.g., NIH Director’s Innovator) providing flexible/no-strings support for high-risk high-reward research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supports innovative research and leadership but coexistence of track-record-focused awards indicates continued conservatism among funders; balance of risk portfolio needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritise early-career researchers (ECR-focused awards)
rubrics_metrics.description: Tailor mechanisms (e.g., New Innovator, Early Independence awards) to fund early-stage researchers and reduce barriers to independence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aimed at promoting innovation and career stability for ECRs; positive long-term outcomes suggested but requires targeted design and safeguarding of fairness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Delphi process for application scoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt (modified) Delphi methods to iteratively solicit expert feedback and converge on selection decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used successfully (e.g., NCI, Cancer Council NSW) to reduce political pressure, groupthink and encourage novel thinking; particularly useful for niche/complex areas and can improve reviewer accessibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modified lottery / randomisation in allocation
rubrics_metrics.description: Incorporate modified lotteries or randomisation (e.g., EPSRC sandpits, HRCNZ modified lottery) to prioritise proposals when other criteria are comparable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Can help prioritise proposals fairly when criteria are similar and reduce bias; may be controversial and requires clear communication of rationale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sandpits and interactive selection processes
rubrics_metrics.description: Use interactive, intensive workshops ('sandpits') to generate, refine and select proposals collaboratively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for interdisciplinary or solution-focused calls to foster collaboration and identify promising approaches; resource-intensive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improve and broaden metrics (include altmetrics)
rubrics_metrics.description: Combine traditional metrics (citation index, journal impact) with alternative metrics (social media outputs, other indicators) to better reflect researcher activity and impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NSF recommends broader metric access and reproducibility; requires aligned infrastructure and funder collaboration to avoid bias and allow verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Increase duration of funded grants
rubrics_metrics.description: Offer longer grant durations (e.g., extend from 3 to 5 years) to improve career stability and research continuity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended by RCUK as part of measures to support career stability; may require budgetary and portfolio adjustments.

rubrics_metrics.name: HEI application quotas and related demand management
rubrics_metrics.description: Limit number of applications per institution to decrease demand on funders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Can reduce submissions but risks concentrating decisions at institutional level and may disadvantage smaller institutions; implementation needs safeguards to avoid unfair internal selection processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit resubmissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Restrict number of times an applicant may resubmit proposals to reduce reviewer and administrative load.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of RCUK proposals to reduce burden; must balance opportunities for improvement with limiting repeated low-value resubmissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outline bid / triage stage to reduce full proposal reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Introduce an initial outline/triage stage to screen proposals before full application submission and review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Can substantially reduce reviewer burden by limiting full reviews to shortlisted proposals; design of triage criteria is critical to fairness and effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create research repositories for reviewer performance assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Build repositories/databases of researcher outputs and performance to aid reviewer assessment and selection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples (Lattes, Researchfish) show potential for structured, reproducible data to inform decisions; requires standardisation and data-sharing agreements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use bibliometrics to detect/adjust for reviewer conflict of interest or bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Correlate reviewer scores with applicants’ bibliometric data to detect possible conflicts of interest or systematic bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simulations (SRA) suggest potential to monitor impartiality, but bibliometrics cannot fully replace good peer review practices and centralized high-quality data are prerequisites.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publish reviewer identities, diversify panels, and independent monitoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Increase transparency by publicising reviewer identities and funding rates, enforce rotation, prevent conflicts of interest, and monitor impartiality independently (AMRC core principles).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Audits showed implementation led to stronger conflict-of-interest policies and greater transparency; however, publicising identities may affect reviewer willingness and requires careful policy design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tailored algorithms/network-flow matching between reviewers and proposals
rubrics_metrics.description: Use tailored matching algorithms (e.g., network flow theory) that incorporate funder guidelines to assign reviewers to proposals without conflicts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pilots reported successful, balanced matches (e.g., SRDA) and administrative efficiency, but evidence on resulting review quality is limited and broader implementation outcomes are uncertain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Large-reviewer-number approaches to minimise chance (e.g., 11 reviewers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assign very large numbers of independent reviewers to individual applications to reduce the role of chance and outlier influence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Studies (McGill) show improved reliability with many reviewers but administrative costs and feasibility make this impractical for most funders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combine shortened and anonymised proposals to reduce selection bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Use shortened application formats together with anonymisation to reduce emphasis on applicant track record and selection bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perceived to reduce bias in pilots and to expedite review, but generalisability and benchmark measures for success need validation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support mechanisms (Delphi, randomisation, golden tickets) to reduce groupthink and selection bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Employ techniques such as the Delphi method, randomisation, or reviewer championing to reduce groupthink and promote diverse decision-making.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evidence suggests these approaches can reduce selection bias and increase review efficiency in specialised fields; may be best used in combination and tailored to context.
